question.text: What will the EU aggregate gas storage filling level be for gas day 12 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the EU-aggregate gas storage filling level that Gas Infrastructure Europe's AGSI+ platform reports for gas day 12 November 2026 (AGSI+ labels this gas day "2026-11-12"; AGSI+ gas days run 06:00–06:00 CET). The resolving value is the "full" field of the AGSI+ dataset "EU" — the filling level as a percentage of working gas volume — for the entry whose gas day is 2026-11-12, taken from AGSI+'s first publication of that gas day's data (expected on 13 November 2026), readable in the AGSI+ API at https://agsi.gie.eu/api?type=eu&size=5 or at the EU page of the AGSI+ data overview https://agsi.gie.eu/data-overview/EU. Any later revision of that gas day's figure is disregarded. If AGSI+ has not published a figure for gas day 2026-11-12 at the time of resolution, the question resolves using the first figure published for that gas day.
question.fine_print: The AGSI+ "EU" dataset is GIE's aggregate of storage facilities located in EU member states; the separate "Europe" aggregate (which adds the UK, Ukraine, Serbia and other non-EU facilities) is not used. AGSI+ publishes filling level as a percentage of working gas volume, and answers are on that same scale: an AGSI+ "full" figure of 74.64 corresponds to an answer of 74.64. Whether AGSI+ marks the gas-day-12 figure as estimated ("E") or confirmed ("C") does not affect resolution.

research:
I couldn't read the resolving figure directly: the AGSI+ API needs a key. Trackers that copy AGSI+ put EU storage at about 74.6% for gas days 30-31 October. A cold snap that began around 1 November is the main thing that will move the 12 November figure.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: The AGSI+ API link (https://agsi.gie.eu/api?type=eu&size=5) answered "access denied, Invalid or missing API key", with no data. The data-overview page did not show any numbers when fetched (it loads them in the browser). [AGSI+](https://agsi.gie.eu/data-overview/EU)
- 2026-10-31 (gas day): The Swiss Energy Dashboard, which uses AGSI+ data, shows the EU at **74.6%**, about 845 TWh. [energiedashboard.admin.ch](https://energiedashboard.admin.ch/gas/eu-gasspeicher)
- 2026-10-30 (gas day): Voltstack shows 74.7% (846 of 1,133 TWh), against 82.8% a year earlier and a five-year average of 89.8%. The question background gives 74.64% for the same day. [Voltstack](https://voltstack.energy/insights/eu-gas-storage-tracker-winter-2026)
- 2026-11-01 update: EnergyRiskIQ shows 74.6% with a "+0.10 pp" daily change, and its withdrawal figures contradict each other (1,535 GWh/d in one place, 748 GWh/d "refill" in another). The gas day it refers to is unclear, so I treat it as low quality. [EnergyRiskIQ](https://energyriskiq.com/gas-storage-levels-in-europe)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Ten gas days remain, and the level starts at about 74.6%.
- The range runs from 68 to 77. Getting above about 75% would take net injections during a cold spell, which is unlikely. Getting to 68% would take an average fall of about 0.5 pp/day, which is roughly 5.9 TWh/day of net withdrawals.
- Conversion: 1 TWh/day of net withdrawal is about 0.088 pp/day.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-01: Germany missed its legal 70% target for 1 November, at about 61.2-61.4% (AGSI data). The regulator and the ministry say supply is secure. [tagesschau](https://www.tagesschau.de/wirtschaft/energie/gasspeicher-vorgaben-ziel-verfehlt-100.html)
- 2026-11-01: RIA Novosti, using GIE data, reports Europe at 74.68%, the lowest for the date since records began in 2011 and 15.09 pp below the 2021-25 average of 89.77%. [RIA](https://ria.ru/20261101/gaz-2128413082.html)
- About 2026-10-30/31: Bloomberg (via Energy Connects) says a cold snap is setting in, with below-normal temperatures and possible frost in southern and eastern Germany. High pressure may also cut wind and solar output, which raises gas burn for power. TTF futures went above €100/MWh for the first time since 2022. [Energy Connects](https://www.energyconnects.com/news/gas-lng/2026/november/germany-misses-gas-storage-target-as-cold-snap-sets-in/)
- Late October 2026: Parts of continental Europe were forecast 2-3°C below normal from the weekend of 31 Oct-1 Nov. The article gives no duration. [ZeroHedge](https://www.zerohedge.com/energy/europe-faces-early-winter-stress-test-cold-snap-looms-natgas-prices-near-triple-digits)
- 2026-10-29: Bloomberg (via Naturalnews) reports TTF above €97/MWh. [Naturalnews](https://www.naturalnews.com/2026-10-29-europe-faces-early-winter-stress-test.html)
- IEEFA: storage may deliver 7.3 bcm less than last winter, and winter demand may need to fall about 7%. [IEEFA](https://ieefa.org/resources/eu-may-need-cut-winter-gas-demand-7-gas-storage-record-seasonal-low)

## 4. Base rates
- 2025: EU storage was 82.8% on 31 October. TASS, citing GIE data, gave 81.17% around 18 November, which is only about 1.6 pp lost in about 18 days. It then fell below 80% on 21 November after a mid-November cold spell. [Energy Outlook Advisors](https://anasalhajjieoa.substack.com/p/eus-gas-import-mix-us-remained-the), [TASS](https://tass.com/economy/2046363/amp), [TASS](https://tass.com/economy/2048027/amp)
- Argus: November 2025 withdrawals averaged 2.8 TWh/d (about 0.25 pp/day), against a five-year November average of 2.4 TWh/d (about 0.21 pp/day). The first half of November usually runs below the monthly average. [Argus](https://www.argusmedia.com/pt/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2760842-eu-gas-stocks-at-four-year-low-on-1-december)
- Last 2026 data point: about -0.13 pp/day (1.49 TWh/d) on 30 October, before the cold arrived (per the question background).
- Projecting 13 days from 74.64%:
  - at -0.13 pp/day: about 72.9%
  - at -0.21 pp/day (the five-year November average): about 71.9%
  - at -0.3 pp/day: about 70.7%
- High prices (about €100/MWh) and record-low stocks may make shippers more cautious about withdrawing. That is speculation; I found no data on it.
- I could not verify exact 12 November figures for 2022-2025.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the Kalshi or Polymarket markets supplied matches this question. They cover US gasoline, Henry Hub and EU diesel stocks.
- A Mantic forecast for the EU level on 1 November said 74.82%. That is a different date. [Mantic](https://app.mantic.com/public/54I6i9oobHV7eq2ApKpQfw)
- Third-party trackers put the EU near 71% by 23 November (per the question background; I did not verify this).
- I found no expert point forecast for 12 November.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 1-12 November: how deep and how long the cold snap lasts. ECMWF forecasts pointed to a possible polar-vortex disturbance and wind reversal around 9 November (per the background), which could push the last few gas days of the window toward steep withdrawals.
- Low wind and solar output under high pressure would raise gas burn for power.
- LNG sendout: disruption around Hormuz and competition from Asian buyers.
- The way TTF prices move between days could affect how much gas is withdrawn versus imported.
- 13 November: AGSI+ first publishes gas day 2026-11-12. AGSI+ revises figures later, and only the first publication counts.

Sources: [AGSI+](https://agsi.gie.eu/data-overview/EU), [energiedashboard.admin.ch](https://energiedashboard.admin.ch/gas/eu-gasspeicher), [Voltstack](https://voltstack.energy/insights/eu-gas-storage-tracker-winter-2026), [EnergyRiskIQ](https://energyriskiq.com/gas-storage-levels-in-europe), [Energy Connects](https://www.energyconnects.com/news/gas-lng/2026/november/germany-misses-gas-storage-target-as-cold-snap-sets-in/), [ZeroHedge](https://www.zerohedge.com/energy/europe-faces-early-winter-stress-test-cold-snap-looms-natgas-prices-near-triple-digits), [Naturalnews](https://www.naturalnews.com/2026-10-29-europe-faces-early-winter-stress-test.html), [tagesschau](https://www.tagesschau.de/wirtschaft/energie/gasspeicher-vorgaben-ziel-verfehlt-100.html), [RIA](https://ria.ru/20261101/gaz-2128413082.html), [IEEFA](https://ieefa.org/resources/eu-may-need-cut-winter-gas-demand-7-gas-storage-record-seasonal-low), [TASS](https://tass.com/economy/2046363/amp), [TASS](https://tass.com/economy/2048027/amp), [Argus](https://www.argusmedia.com/pt/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2760842-eu-gas-stocks-at-four-year-low-on-1-december), [Energy Outlook Advisors](https://anasalhajjieoa.substack.com/p/eus-gas-import-mix-us-remained-the), [Mantic](https://app.mantic.com/public/54I6i9oobHV7eq2ApKpQfw)

The newest figure I could find is about 74.6-74.7% for gas day 30 October 2026, with daily withdrawals so far small (about 0.1 pp/day). A colder spell forecast for early November is the main thing that could speed up the decline before 12 November.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: The AGSI+ API (`api?type=eu`) returned "access denied: Invalid or missing API key", and the data-overview page showed only navigation, no numbers. I could not read the official series. [AGSI+ API](https://agsi.gie.eu/api?type=eu&size=10)
- Gas day 2026-10-30 (newest found): the question background gives 74.64% (845.5 TWh, about -0.13 pp that day). Other sources quoting AGSI give slightly different numbers:
  - RIA Novosti says 74.68%, with about 0.09 pp withdrawn that day. [RIA](https://ria.ru/20261101/gaz-2128413082.html)
  - Voltstack says 74.7% (846 TWh). [Voltstack](https://voltstack.energy/insights/eu-gas-storage-tracker-winter-2026)
  - These small gaps may be revisions or rounding. Only the first published figure counts for resolution.
- I found no published EU figures for gas days 31 October or 1 November. Bloomberg noted official 1 November data would only come after the weekend. [Energy Connects/Bloomberg](https://www.energyconnects.com/news/gas-lng/2026/november/germany-misses-gas-storage-target-as-cold-snap-sets-in/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The value is about 10 gas days away.
- The 30 October level was a record low for that date. It was about 15.1 pp below the 2021-25 average of 89.77% and below the five-year minimum of 77.0%. [RIA](https://ria.ru/20261101/gaz-2128413082.html), [Voltstack](https://voltstack.energy/insights/eu-gas-storage-tracker-winter-2026)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-01: Germany was at 61.17-61.4%, missing its 70% target for 1 November. The ministry and the Federal Network Agency say winter supply is still secure. [Tagesschau](https://www.tagesschau.de/wirtschaft/energie/gasspeicher-vorgaben-ziel-verfehlt-100.html)
- 2026-11-01 (Bloomberg): Colder weather is forecast across Germany and much of Europe "in the coming days".
  - Vaisala expects Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich to run 2-4°C below normal.
  - The German weather service (DWD) expects frost in the south and east.
  - A high-pressure "Dunkelflaute" (calm, cloudy, little wind) is likely, which pushes up gas burn for power.
  - TTF futures went above €100/MWh last week, the first time since 2022. [Energy Connects](https://www.energyconnects.com/news/gas-lng/2026/november/germany-misses-gas-storage-target-as-cold-snap-sets-in/)
- 2026-11-01: RIA reports Europe switched to net withdrawal in mid-October, with the first positive net withdrawal on 20 October. The EU lowered the 1 November target from 90% to 80% in June 2026. [RIA](https://ria.ru/20261101/gaz-2128413082.html)
- 2026-10-28: Global Energy Flow gives 74.93% for gas day 26 October, up 0.02 pp that day (injection 1,257 GWh/d, withdrawal 1,095 GWh/d). [GEF](https://global-energy-flow.com/storage/trajectory/)
- Late October: ACER said storage was 75% full as of 21 October. [ACER](https://www.acer.europa.eu/news/eu-gas-storage-75-filled)
- IEEFA estimates the EU may need about a 7% cut in winter gas demand. [IEEFA](https://ieefa.org/resources/eu-may-need-cut-winter-gas-demand-7-gas-storage-record-seasonal-low)

## 4. Base rates
- 2025: about 83% on 1 November and 81.17% around 18-20 November. That is roughly -0.1 pp/day, with withdrawals starting late (mid-November). [TASS](https://tass.com/economy/2046363/amp), [ACER](https://www.acer.europa.eu/sites/default/files/documents/Publications/2026-ACER-Gas-Key-Developments-winter.pdf)
- 2021, 2022 and 2024 below are from my own memory. I did not verify them in this session.
  - 2024: about 95.3% on 1 November to about 93% on 12 November (about -0.2 pp/day, during a Dunkelflaute).
  - 2023 and 2022: roughly flat or slightly up through mid-November.
  - 2021 (a low-stock year): about 77% to about 75% (about -0.2 pp/day).
- Over 1-12 November, recent years have ranged from about +0.5 pp to about -2.5 pp.
- Recent 2026 pace: +0.3 pp in the week to 26 October, then about -0.1 pp/day.
- From 74.64%, 13 days at:

| Daily change | Level on 12 November |
|---|---|
| -0.13 pp | about 72.9% |
| -0.2 pp | about 72.0% |
| -0.3 pp | about 70.7% |

- In very cold spells, single-day falls can exceed 0.3 pp. Early January 2026 saw withdrawals above 3.5 TWh/day (about 0.3 pp/day). [VT Markets](https://www.vtmarkets.com/en-ca/?p=38584)

## 5. Other forecasts
- No Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market matches this question. The Kalshi markets supplied (US gasoline, Henry Hub, Tesla storage) and the Polymarket EU diesel market are not relevant.
- Expert views and projections:
  - The question background cites third-party trackers putting the EU at about 71% by 23 November. I did not verify this.
  - Global Energy Flow, as of 28 October, only projected to 1 November, giving about 75.1-75.9%. That projection is already outdated. [GEF](https://global-energy-flow.com/storage/trajectory/)
  - I found no published point forecast for 12 November.
- Data-quality warning: EnergyRiskIQ shows 74.6% with "+0.10 pp" and 748 GWh/day of injections, which conflicts with the other sources. Treat it as unreliable. [EnergyRiskIQ](https://energyriskiq.com/gas-storage-levels-in-europe)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- First week of November: the forecast cold, low-wind spell in Germany and Central Europe. Higher heating demand and gas use in power would push withdrawals up. [Energy Connects](https://www.energyconnects.com/news/gas-lng/2026/november/germany-misses-gas-storage-target-as-cold-snap-sets-in/)
- Around 9 November: the possible polar-vortex disturbance or wind reversal mentioned in the question background. I did not verify this. Any cold that follows typically arrives with a lag of 1-3 weeks, so most of it may land after 12 November.
- LNG arrivals and the Strait of Hormuz situation, plus TTF prices (around €95-100+/MWh). High prices may cut industrial demand and draw in LNG cargoes.
- AGSI+ data releases for gas days 31 October to 12 November. The resolving figure is the first publication, expected on 13 November.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 11 days. Gas day 12 November is first published on about 13 November, and resolution is around 13 November.

(b) **Latest known value:** 74.64% on gas day 30 October 2026, from AGSI+ via the question background. Trackers show about 74.6% for 31 October.

(c) **If nothing changed:** About 74.6%.

(d) **If the current trend continued:**
- At the pre-cold rate of -0.13 pp/day: about 72.9%.
- The cold snap that began around 1 November, with low wind and frost, likely lifts withdrawals to about 2.5-4 TWh/d, which is 0.22-0.35 pp/day. That implies about 70.5-72%.
- The five-year November average of -0.21 pp/day gives about 71.9%.

(e) **Historical variation:** Over 12-13 early-November days, the EU level typically falls 1-4 pp. In 2025 it fell only about 1.6 pp in 18 days, while cold early Novembers have produced 3-5 pp. Daily changes range from small net injections to about -0.45 pp.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:**
- Trackers put the level near 71% by 23 November, which implies a modest pace and would mean about 72-72.5% on 12 November.
- No markets cover this quantity.
- Very high TTF prices, at €100/MWh or more, draw in LNG. Record-low stocks may make shippers somewhat cautious about withdrawing.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** A deep, persistent cold and windless spell from 1 November is amplified by early polar-vortex effects. Withdrawals average about 5 TWh/d, which takes the level to about 69%.
- **High:** The cold snap is brief and gives way to mild, windy Atlantic weather. Strong LNG sendout brings net flows near zero, and the level holds around 74%.

I put the median at about 72.0%.

- In 2025, only about 1 to 1.5 pp was lost.

(f) **Expectations of experts and markets:**
- No direct market prices this quantity.
- Trackers project about 71% by 23 November, which implies roughly 72% around 12 November.
- High TTF prices and record-low stocks may make shippers somewhat cautious about withdrawing.
- The polar-vortex effect around 9 November would mostly reach the surface after 12 November.
